Assessment of BA.evidence_source: The introduction discusses the Body Appreciation Scale (BAS) and Body Appreciation Scale-2 (BAS-2) as instruments used across multiple studies cited in the literature. The text states: 'The construct was originally measured using the Body Appreciation Scale (BAS), a 13-item measure' and later 'Tylka and Wood-Barcalow (2015b) refined the BAS by deleting several poor-performing items and developing additional items that better reflected the concept of positive body image, as contemporaneously understood. The result of this refinement was the Body Appreciation Scale-2 (BAS-2), a 10 item measure.' Both instruments are discussed as assessment tools used in the reviewed literature.

section_summary.extract_value: This is an introductory literature review section that discusses the development and validation of body appreciation measures, specifically the Body Appreciation Scale (BAS) and its refined version, the Body Appreciation Scale-2 (BAS-2). The section reviews evidence for the one-dimensional factor structure of BAS-2 across multiple countries and cultural groups, examines sex invariance and differences, and summarizes construct validity evidence showing positive associations with well-being measures and mixed associations with BMI. No specific study data is reported in this section; rather, it synthesizes findings from numerous cited studies.
